text:
elaine: Heads-up — we need a clear policy + implementation plan for customer-facing audit log visibility. Customer asked for a 'delegated auditor' role that can only view logs for specific projects within a tenant. Current model: org_admin sees all tenant events; member sees only their own events. Thoughts?

ajay: Do we already partition audit events by tenant_id? I know the DB has tenant_id, but our daily exports to S3 sometimes bundle across tenants for retention/debug. :thinking_face:

maria: We do store tenant_id on audit_events. The export pipeline currently flattens into one file/day per-region for retention to save object counts. We can change to per-tenant prefixes in S3 and lock down access via IAM policies — low friction for customer-facing exports.

tyler: For live UI/API visibility we should enforce RBAC checks in the audit service. Suggested roles: org_admin, tenant_auditor, project_auditor, member. Tokens should support scopes like `audit.read:tenant:<tenant_id>` and `audit.read:project:<project_id>`.

ajay: Agree. Also need schema changes before we expose more fields to customers: add `actor_type`, `actor_id`, `actor_email_redacted` (bool), `sensitive` (bool) for PII-bearing events, plus `event_version`/`schema_version`.

elaine: Customer-facing validation: they want a machine-readable event sample and a validation endpoint so UI and exports only accept/render events that match the contract. Propose `/audit/validate` that returns errors/warnings for events.

compliance: KMS note — today we use an org-level key for audit logs at rest. If we move to per-tenant exports and scoped auditor tokens, we need either per-tenant CMKs or a re-encryption flow on export. Key policy must allow an auditor role to decrypt reads but not re-encrypt for other tenants.

audit-bot: New RFC created: `rfc/audit-log-tenant-scope.md` — please review and comment. :robot_face:

maria: Edge cases to call out: admin 'view-as'/impersonation must be explicit in the audit trail (`admin_impersonation` event) and should be filtered unless the auditor role has explicit permission. Also decide how service accounts background jobs are scoped — project-scoped service accounts vs org-scoped.

tyler: Implementation plan (rough):
- Phase 1 (2w): API token scoping + RBAC checks on audit endpoints + S3 per-tenant prefixes (no KMS change).
- Phase 2 (2w): Schema bump + validation endpoint + UI filters + exports change.
- Phase 3 (3-4w): KMS per-tenant keys + key policy updates + access review automation.

elaine: Can we ship Phase 1 without touching KMS? Customer asked for delegated auditor within 3 weeks.

compliance: Phase 1 ok as long as exports don't leak cross-tenant data and audit service enforces token scopes. We'll require an internal review of the export lambda and a short design doc for key plans in Phase 3.

ajay: I'll open a PR to add token scopes and API guard rails. Will include unit/integration tests for `audit.read:tenant` positive and negative cases.

tyler: I'll prototype S3 layout change and update the retention lambda to write per-tenant prefixes. I'll also draft a migration job to re-process the last 30 days into the new layout.

elaine: Great — thanks. Sync tomorrow 10am to finalize schema fields, RBAC verbs, and approve RFC. Agenda posted in calendar. :calendar:
